# Simulating a Wiener procss model 

```{r}
#| echo: false 

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal())
```

Source: https://sites.me.ucsb.edu/~moehlis/APC591/tutorials/tutorial7/node2.html 

A standard Wiener process^[often called Brownian motion] on the interval $[0, T]$ is a random variable $W(t)$ that depends continuously on $t in [0, T]$ and satisifes the following: 

- $W(0) = 0$ 
- For $0 <= s < t <= T$, 
$$W(t) - W(s) \sim \sqrt{t-s} \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$$
- For $0 <= s < t < u < v <= T$, $W(t) - W(s)$ and $W(v) - W(u)$ are independent. 

To make things easier on a computer, we discretize the Wiener process with a timestamp $d t$ as $$d W \sim \sqrt{d t} \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$$ 

```{r}
T = 1 
N = 500 
dt = T / N 
W <- c(sqrt(dt) * rnorm(1, 0, 1))
for (i in 2:N){
  dW <- sqrt(dt) * rnorm(1, 0, 1)
  W <- c(W, tail(W, n = 1) + dW)
}
```

```{r}
plot(W, type = "l")

W %>% as_tibble(.) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = 1:500, y = value)) + 
  geom_line()
```
